summary.intent: Get Callisto ready for a publish (0.12.0 release): fix the Release verify job and publish diagnostics, check readiness of the version PR #248, and consolidate overlapping pending changesets into a PR stacked on #302.
summary.outcome: Release workflow verify job is fixed and #302 (publish stdout visibility) is nearly merged; readiness was assessed (#248 has no checks, misleading body). A consolidation PR rewriting/removing changesets was created and stacked on #302, validated with Callisto's status check, though its final push/PR result isn't shown.

repo: Callisto's release flow uses a bot-maintained version PR (#248, branch callisto/version-packages) that regenerates whenever changesets on main change.

Commits pushed by the workflow's own token don't trigger CI, so #248 can show 'no checks reported' and may be unmergeable under branch protection until CI is triggered by a person/App token or by close/reopen.
Publish has a 15-minute deadline (timeouts::PUBLISH, 900s); observed hangs ended at 12 and 14.5 minutes because pnpm itself exited.

pnpm prints errors to stdout; npm and Cargo failure messages previously used stderr only, while PyPI's already included stdout. PR #302 unifies this via a shared helper and echoes redacted stdout live during publish runs.
Callisto already runs publish with stdin closed, so a 2FA prompt can't block waiting for input; suspected cause of main-package hang is pnpm 11 not honoring the temporary npm config.
Changesets follow a one-topic-per-entry rule; noble-hawks-drift violated it by mixing shallow clone E315, inline workspace tables, pnpm and nested npm.

0.12.0 includes breaking changes (bare package references rejected E317, report schema v2, release --package qualified-only) but is only a minor bump because the project is pre-1.0; the #248 body wrongly says 'All changes are backward compatible'.
The release-refuses-published-version-on-later-commit guard has known gaps: inherited Cargo versions skipped, provider errors swallowed, history capped at 100 commits.
Release reruns adopt whatever already landed, so re-running a failed job is safe.
Callisto has a status check command usable to validate changesets.
workflow: Batching changeset edits into a single PR avoids repeated regeneration of the version PR and repeated check problems.
Writing multi-step shell logic to script files under /tmp and running them was the pattern used for gh/git operations and bulk changeset rewrites.
Validate bulk rewrites of release metadata with the project's own tooling before committing.

friction: Unexpected merge of #290 against Codex's recommendation to hold it caused a surprise and required re-checking PR and main state.
Base update retries and branch ref inspection were needed when rebuilding the stacked PR on current main.
Entire again pushed checkpoint refs to origin on each commit (unresolved push_sessions concern).
Root cause of michi's pnpm hang remains unknown, blocking certainty about publish reliability.
#248 head had no CI checks, so every changeset change reopens the checks question.
open_items: Merge #302 and #300, then wait for #248 to regenerate, get its checks running and green, and fix the misleading 'backward compatible' line before publishing.
Decide whether to add an idle (no-output) limit for publish versus keeping the 15-minute deadline.
Decide whether to rework #290 or the published-version guard (inherited Cargo versions, swallowed provider errors, 100-commit cap) or reword its changeset.
Confirm the new live stdout in #302 reveals why the main-package pnpm publish hangs; finish 0.4.0 release with a throwaway timeout 180 pnpm publish run.
Callisto's execute step (crates.io publishes, tags, GitHub release with three binaries) is unproven since the verify job broke; first real run is the test.
User still needs to accept ADR 12.
Resolve Entire push_sessions behavior pushing checkpoint refs to origin.
Merge the consolidation PR after #302 and verify #248 matches the 35-to-~25 changeset consolidation.
